mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches what makes a sukkah not kosher: if it is too tall, too short, has fewer than three walls, or has more sun than shade. It also teaches about an "old sukkah" built long before the chag.

chunks.he: סֻכָּה שֶׁהִיא גְבוֹהָה לְמַעְלָה מֵעֶשְׂרִים אַמָּה,
chunks.en: A sukkah that is taller than twenty amos
chunks.st: A sukka, i.e., its roofing, which is the main and most crucial element of the mitzva, that is more than twenty cubits high

words.note: An amah is a measure, about the length of an arm from elbow to fingertip.

chunks.en: is not kosher. Rabbi Yehuda says it is kosher.
chunks.st: is unfit. Rabbi Yehuda deems it fit.

chunks.en: And one that is not ten tefachim tall,
chunks.st: Similarly, a sukka that is not even ten handbreadths high,

words.note: A tefach is a handbreadth, the width of a hand.

chunks.en: and one that does not have three walls,
chunks.st: and one that does not have three walls,

words.en: and one that does not have

chunks.en: and one that has more sun than shade,
chunks.st: and one whose sunlight that passes through its roofing is greater than its shade

chunks.en: is not kosher. An old sukkah:
chunks.st: are unfit. With regard to an old sukka,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is not kosher,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai deem it unfit for the mitzva of sukka

words.note: Beis Shammai are the students of the great Sage Shammai.

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

words.note: Beis Hillel are the students of the great Sage Hillel.

chunks.en: And what is an old sukkah?
chunks.st: And which is considered an old sukka?

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁעֲשָׂאָהּ קֹדֶם לֶחָג שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם.
chunks.en: Any sukkah made thirty days before the chag.
chunks.explain: It was not made for the mitzvah, but for something else.
chunks.st: It is any booth that one established thirty days or more prior to the Festival
chunks.stMore: without expressly designating that it was for the mitzva of sukka. In that case, the assumption is that he constructed it for some other purpose.

chunks.en: But if he made it for the sake of the chag,
chunks.st: However, if he established it expressly for the sake of the festival of Sukkot,

chunks.en: even at the start of the year, it is kosher.
chunks.st: even if he constructed it at the beginning of the previous year, it is fit for use in the fulfillment of the mitzva of sukka, even according to Beit Shammai.

mishnayos.summary: A sukkah under a tree or under another sukkah is not kosher, because its s'chach must be open to the sky. Rabbi Yehuda says when no one can live in the top sukkah, the bottom one is kosher.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his sukkah under a tree,
chunks.st: With regard to one who establishes his sukka beneath a tree,

chunks.en: it is as if he made it inside the house.
chunks.explain: So it is not kosher.
chunks.st: it is as though he established it inside the house
chunks.stMore: and it is unfit.

chunks.en: A sukkah on top of a sukkah:
chunks.st: If one established a sukka atop another sukka,

chunks.en: the top one is kosher,
chunks.st: the upper sukka is fit

chunks.en: and the bottom one is not kosher.
chunks.st: and the lower sukka is unfit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if no one can live in the top one,
chunks.explain: Its floor is too weak to hold people and their things.
chunks.st: If there are no residents in the upper sukka,

chunks.en: the bottom one is kosher.
chunks.st: the lower sukka is fit.

mishnayos.summary: If you spread a sheet over or under the s'chach, or sit under a canopy bed, that spot is not kosher for the sukkah. A low two-post bed cover is allowed.

chunks.en: If he spread a sheet over it because of the sun,
chunks.st: If one spread a sheet over the roofing as protection for those sitting in the sukka due to the sun,

chunks.en: or under it, because of falling leaves,
chunks.st: or if one spread a sheet beneath the roofing as protection due to the falling leaves,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁפֵּרַס עַל גַּבֵּי הַקִּינוֹף, פְּסוּלָה.
chunks.en: or if he spread it over a canopy bed, it is not kosher.
chunks.st: or if one spread a sheet as a canopy over the frame of a four-post [kinof] bed, the area in the sukka beneath the sheets is unfit.
chunks.stMore: In the first two cases, because the sheet is susceptible to ritual impurity, it renders the otherwise fit roofing unfit. In the case of the canopy, one is not sitting under the roofing of the sukka; rather, he is sitting inside a tent.

words.note: A bed with four posts and a cover on top, like a little tent.

chunks.he: אֲבָל פּוֹרֵס הוּא עַל גַּבֵּי נַקְלִיטֵי הַמִּטָּה:
chunks.en: But he may spread it over a bed with two posts.
chunks.explain: Its cover slopes down like a roof, so it is not a real tent.
chunks.st: However, one may spread the sheet over the frame of a two-post [naklitei] bed, which has one post in the middle of each end of the bed. When spreading the sheet over the posts it forms an inclined rather than a flat roof, and a tent with an inclined roof is not considered a significant structure.

words.note: One post at the head and one at the foot of the bed.

mishnayos.summary: Plants still growing from the ground may not be used as s'chach. The rule is: s'chach must grow from the ground and must not be something that can become tamei.

chunks.he: הִדְלָה עָלֶיהָ אֶת הַגֶּפֶן וְאֶת הַדְּלַעַת
chunks.en: If he let a grapevine or a gourd plant climb over it
chunks.st: If one trellised climbing plants such as a grapevine, or gourd plant,

chunks.en: or ivy, and put s'chach on top of them,
chunks.explain: The plants are still attached to the ground.
chunks.st: or ivy [kissos], over a sukka while they were still attached to the ground, and then added roofing atop them,

words.note: S'chach is the covering on top of a sukkah.

chunks.he: פְּסוּלָה. וְאִם הָיָה סִכּוּךְ הַרְבֵּה מֵהֶן,
chunks.en: it is not kosher. But if there was more s'chach than plants,
chunks.st: the sukka is unfit. If the amount of fit roofing was greater than the plants attached to the ground,

chunks.en: or he cut them,
chunks.st: or if he cut the climbing plants so that they were no longer attached to the ground,

chunks.en: it is kosher. This is the rule:
chunks.st: it is fit. This is the principle with regard to the roofing of a sukka:

chunks.en: anything that can become tamei
chunks.st: Anything that is susceptible to ritual impurity, e.g., vessels,

words.note: Tumah is a kind of spiritual impurity.

chunks.en: or does not grow from the ground,
chunks.st: or its growth is not from the ground, e.g., animal hides,

chunks.en: may not be used as s'chach.
chunks.st: one may not roof his sukka with it.

chunks.en: And anything that cannot
chunks.st: And anything that is not

chunks.en: become tamei and grows from the ground,
chunks.st: susceptible to ritual impurity and its growth is from the ground,

chunks.en: may be used as s'chach.
chunks.st: one may roof his sukka with it.

mishnayos.summary: Tied bundles of straw, wood or twigs may not be used as s'chach. Once they are untied they are kosher, and even tied they are fine for walls.

chunks.en: Bundles of straw and bundles of wood
chunks.st: One may not roof a sukka with bundles of straw tied with rope, or bundles of wood,

chunks.en: and bundles of twigs may not be used as s'chach.
chunks.explain: This is when they are tied up.
chunks.st: or bundles of twigs.

chunks.en: And all of them, if he untied them,
chunks.st: And with regard to all of the bundles, if one untied them,

chunks.en: are kosher. And all of them are kosher for walls.
chunks.st: they are fit for use in roofing the sukka, as their lack of fitness is due to the fact that the bundles are tied. And even when tied, all of the bundles are fit for use in constructing the walls of the sukka.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir argue about using boards as s'chach. A wide board on a sukkah is fine, but one may not sleep under it.

chunks.en: We may use boards as s'chach,
chunks.st: One may roof the sukka with boards like those used in the ceiling of a house;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Meir forbids it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir prohibits their use.

chunks.en: If he put on it a board that is
chunks.st: If one placed a board that is

chunks.en: four tefachim wide,
chunks.st: four handbreadths wide atop the sukka,

chunks.en: it is kosher, as long as he does not sleep under it.
chunks.st: the sukka is fit. He fulfills his obligation, provided he does not sleep beneath the board.

mishnayos.summary: A ceiling of boards with no plaster on top can become a kosher sukkah. Beis Shammai, Beis Hillel and Rabbi Meir argue about what one must do to fix it.

chunks.en: A ceiling of boards that has no plaster on it:
chunks.st: In the case of a roof made of boards that are four handbreadths wide upon which there is no coat of plaster,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says
chunks.stMore: that Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagree with regard to the manner in which to render it fit.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he moves each board and takes out one from between each two.
chunks.explain: He puts kosher s'chach in its place.
chunks.st: One moves each board, and then it is considered as though he placed the board there for the sake of the mitzva of sukka, and one then removes one board from among the boards and replaces it with fit roofing.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he moves them or takes out one from between.
chunks.st: One need not perform both actions; rather, one must either move the boards or remove one from among them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he takes out one from between,
chunks.st: One only removes one from among them

chunks.en: and does not need to move them.
chunks.st: and does not move the others.

mishnayos.summary: Metal spits or bed boards on a sukkah are fine if there are equal spaces between them filled with kosher s'chach. A hole dug into a stack of grain is not a sukkah.

chunks.he: הַמְקָרֶה סֻכָּתוֹ בְשַׁפּוּדִין אוֹ בַאֲרֻכּוֹת הַמִּטָּה,
chunks.en: Someone who roofs his sukkah with spits or with the long boards of a bed,
chunks.st: In the case of one who roofs his sukka with metal skewers or with the long boards of the bed,
chunks.stMore: which compose its frame,

words.note: Long metal sticks used for roasting meat.

chunks.en: if the space between them is as wide as they are,
chunks.explain: And he puts kosher s'chach in the spaces.
chunks.st: if there is space between each one of them equal to the width of the skewers or the boards, and if he places fit roofing in those spaces,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה. הַחוֹטֵט בְּגָדִישׁ לַעֲשׂוֹת בּוֹ סֻכָּה,
chunks.en: it is kosher. Someone who digs into a stack of grain to make a sukkah in it,
chunks.st: the sukka is fit. In the case of one who hollows out and creates a space inside a stack of grain, to construct a sukka in it

chunks.en: it is not a sukkah.
chunks.explain: The roof was not made; it was there already.
chunks.st: it is not a sukka.

mishnayos.summary: Walls that hang down from the top must come within three tefachim of the ground. Walls built up from the ground must be ten tefachim tall. The s'chach must not be three tefachim away from the walls.

chunks.en: Someone who hangs walls from the top down,
chunks.st: One who lowers the walls of the sukka from up downward,

chunks.he: אִם גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים, פְּסוּלָה.
chunks.en: if the wall is three tefachim above the ground, it is not kosher.
chunks.explain: Animals could go in under the wall.
chunks.st: if the lower edge of the wall is three handbreadths above the ground, the sukka is unfit.
chunks.stMore: Since animals can enter through that space, it is not the wall of a fit sukka.

chunks.en: From the bottom up,
chunks.st: However, if one constructs the wall from down upward,

chunks.he: אִם גָּבוֹהַּ מִן הָאָרֶץ עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים, כְּשֵׁרָה.
chunks.en: if the wall is ten tefachim high from the ground, it is kosher.
chunks.st: if the wall is ten handbreadths high, even if it does not reach the roofing, the sukka is fit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: just as from the bottom up it must be ten tefachim,
chunks.st: Just as a wall built from down upward must be ten handbreadths,

chunks.en: so from the top down it must be ten tefachim.
chunks.st: so too, in a case where one lowers the wall from up downward, it must be ten handbreadths in length.
chunks.stMore: Regardless of its height off the ground, it is the wall of a fit sukka, as the legal status of a ten-handbreadth partition is that of a full-fledged partition in all areas of halakha.

chunks.en: If he put the s'chach away from
chunks.st: If one distanced the roofing from the walls

chunks.en: the walls by three tefachim, it is not kosher.
chunks.st: of the sukka at a distance of three handbreadths the sukka is unfit, because three handbreadths of open space, even adjacent to the walls, render the sukka unfit.

mishnayos.summary: If the s'chach is far from the walls, with a regular roof in between, the sukkah is kosher only if the gap is less than four amos. The same is true for a big sukkah with bad s'chach around its edges.

chunks.en: A house whose roof broke, and he put s'chach over the hole,
chunks.st: In the case of a house that was breached, creating a hole in the middle of the roof, and one roofed over the breach,

chunks.en: if from the wall
chunks.st: if from the wall

chunks.en: to the s'chach there are four amos, it is not kosher.
chunks.explain: If it is less than four amos, the sukkah is kosher.
chunks.st: to the roofing there are four or more cubits of the remaining original roof, it is an unfit sukka.
chunks.stMore: If the roofing is less than four cubits from the wall, the sukka is fit, based on the principle of curved wall; the remaining intact ceiling is considered an extension of the vertical wall.

chunks.en: And the same for a yard with a porch roof around it.
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of a courtyard that is surrounded on three sides by a portico,
chunks.stMore: which has a roof but no walls, if one placed roofing over the courtyard between the different sides of the portico and the roof of the portico is four cubits wide, the sukka is unfit.

words.note: A roof held up by posts, with no walls.

chunks.en: A big sukkah
chunks.st: Similarly, a large sukka

chunks.en: that had something around it that may not be used as s'chach,
chunks.st: that was surrounded at the edge of its roofing with material with which one may not roof a sukka, e.g., vessels susceptible to ritual impurity,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ תַּחְתָּיו אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, פְּסוּלָה:
chunks.en: if there are four amos under it, it is not kosher.
chunks.st: if there are four cubits beneath the unfit roofing, the sukka is unfit. The principle of curved wall does not apply to unfit roofing that measures four cubits or more.

mishnayos.summary: The Sages argue if a sukkah shaped like a tent with no flat roof is kosher. A reed mat may be used as s'chach only if it was made for s'chach and not for lying on.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his sukkah shaped like a pointed hut,
chunks.st: One who establishes his sukka like a type of circular hut,
chunks.stMore: with no roof whose walls slope down from the center

chunks.en: or leans it against a wall,
chunks.st: or who rested the sukka against the wall,
chunks.stMore: by taking long branches and placing one end on the ground and leaning the other end against the wall to establish a structure with no roof,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says it is not kosher,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer deems it unfit

chunks.en: because it has no roof.
chunks.st: because it does not have a roof,

chunks.en: But the Sages say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis deem it fit;
chunks.stMore: as, in their opinion, the roof and the walls may be a single entity, indistinguishable from each other.

chunks.en: A big mat made of reeds:
chunks.st: In the case of a large mat of reeds,

chunks.en: if he made it for lying on,
chunks.st: if one initially produced it for the purpose of lying upon it,

chunks.en: it can become tamei, and may not be used as s'chach.
chunks.st: it is susceptible to ritual impurity like any other vessel, and therefore one may not roof a sukka with it.

chunks.he: לְסִכּוּךְ, מְסַכְּכִין בָּהּ וְאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה.
chunks.en: If he made it for s'chach, it may be used as s'chach, and it cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: If one initially produced it for roofing, one may roof a sukka with it, and it is not susceptible to ritual impurity,
chunks.stMore: as its legal status is not that of a vessel.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says
chunks.stMore: that the distinction between mats is based on use, not size.

chunks.en: whether it is small or big,
chunks.st: Therefore, with regard to both a small mat and a large mat,

chunks.en: if he made it for lying on,
chunks.st: if one produced it for the purpose of lying upon it,

chunks.en: it can become tamei, and may not be used as s'chach.
chunks.st: it is susceptible to ritual impurity and one may not roof a sukka with it.

chunks.he: לְסִכּוּךְ, מְסַכְּכִין בָּהּ וְאֵינָהּ מְקַבֶּלֶת טֻמְאָה:
chunks.en: If he made it for s'chach, it may be used as s'chach, and it cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: If one produced it for roofing, one may roof a sukka with it, and it is not susceptible to ritual impurity.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who sleeps under a bed in the sukkah has not done the mitzvah. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon tell stories that show what the Elders thought.

chunks.en: Someone who sleeps under the bed in the sukkah
chunks.st: One who sleeps beneath the bed in the sukka

chunks.en: has not done his mitzvah.
chunks.explain: The bed is like a tent between him and the s'chach.
chunks.st: did not fulfill his obligation,
chunks.stMore: because the bed constitutes a tent that serves as a barrier between him and the roofing of the sukka.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: we used to do this:
chunks.st: It was our custom

chunks.he: שֶׁהָיִינוּ יְשֵׁנִים תַּחַת הַמִּטָּה בִּפְנֵי הַזְּקֵנִים,
chunks.en: we would sleep under the bed in front of the Elders,
chunks.st: that we would sleep beneath the bed before the Elders

chunks.en: and they did not say anything to us.
chunks.st: and they did not say anything to us
chunks.stMore: to the effect that we are not fulfilling our obligation. Apparently, the halakhic status of the bed is not like that of a tent and it does not prevent fulfillment of the mitzva.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: § Rabbi Shimon said, contrary to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda:

chunks.en: Once, Tavi, the servant of Rabban
chunks.st: There was an incident involving Tavi, the Canaanite slave of

chunks.en: Gamliel, was sleeping under the bed.
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel, who was sleeping beneath the bed,

words.note: The leader of the Jewish people in his time.

chunks.en: And Rabban Gamliel said to the Elders,
chunks.st: and Rabban Gamliel lightheartedly said to the Elders:

chunks.en: "Did you see my servant Tavi?
chunks.st: Did you see my slave Tavi,

chunks.en: He is a Torah scholar, and he knows
chunks.st: who is a Torah scholar and knows

words.note: A talmid chacham is a Torah scholar.

chunks.en: that servants do not have to keep the mitzvah of sukkah.
chunks.st: that slaves are exempt from the mitzva of sukka?
chunks.stMore: Since it is a positive, time-bound mitzva, Canaanite slaves, whose status with regard to this halakhic category is like that of women, are exempt from the obligation to fulfill the mitzva of sukka.

chunks.en: That is why he sleeps under the bed."
chunks.st: Therefore, he sleeps under the bed.

chunks.en: And from his words, by the way, we learned
chunks.explain: Rabban Gamliel was not trying to teach a halacha.
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon continued: And by the way, as Rabban Gamliel was not issuing a halakhic ruling, we learned

chunks.en: that someone who sleeps under the bed
chunks.st: that one who sleeps beneath the bed

chunks.en: has not done his mitzvah.
chunks.st: did not fulfill his obligation.

mishnayos.summary: A sukkah leaning on a bed is kosher, but Rabbi Yehuda says it must stand by itself. A sukkah with messy s'chach, or very thick s'chach, is kosher as long as it gives more shade than sun.

chunks.en: Someone who leans his sukkah on the legs of a bed,
chunks.st: One who supports his sukka on the legs of the bed,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he leans the sukka roofing on a bed,

chunks.en: it is kosher. Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: the sukka is fit. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אִם אֵינָהּ יְכוֹלָה לַעֲמֹד בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ,
chunks.en: if it cannot stand up by itself,
chunks.st: If the sukka cannot stand in and of itself without support of the bed,

chunks.en: it is not kosher. A sukkah with messy s'chach,
chunks.explain: The s'chach is not even; some is higher and some lower.
chunks.st: it is unfit. A sukka that is meduvlelet
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz leaves the word untranslated; the meaning follows Bartenura.

chunks.en: and that has more shade than sun,
chunks.st: and whose shade exceeds its sunlight

chunks.en: is kosher. One with s'chach as thick as a house,
chunks.st: is fit. A sukka whose roofing is thick like a house of sorts,

chunks.en: even though
chunks.st: even though

words.note: Af al pi means "even though."

chunks.en: the stars cannot be seen from inside it, is kosher.
chunks.st: it is so thick that the stars cannot be seen from within it, is fit.

mishnayos.summary: A sukkah on a wagon, boat, tree or camel is kosher. But on Yom Tov we may not climb a tree or use an animal, so we may not go up into a sukkah that needs the tree to hold it up.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his sukkah on top of a wagon
chunks.st: In the case of one who establishes his sukka at the top of the wagon

chunks.en: or on top of a ship,
chunks.st: or at the top of the ship,

chunks.en: it is kosher, and we may go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: although it is portable it is fit, as it is sufficient for a sukka to be a temporary residence. And one may ascend and enter it even on the first Festival day.

chunks.he: בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן אוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי גָמָל,
chunks.en: On top of a tree or on a camel,
chunks.st: In the case of one who establishes his sukka at the top of a tree or atop a camel,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
chunks.en: it is kosher, but we may not go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: The Rabbis said not to climb trees or use animals on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the sukka is fit, but one may not ascend and enter it on the first Festival day
chunks.stMore: because the Sages prohibit climbing or using trees or animals on the Festival.

chunks.en: If two walls are in the tree and one is made by a person,
chunks.st: If two of the walls of the sukka are in the tree and one is established on the ground by a person,

chunks.he: אוֹ שְׁתַּיִם בִּידֵי אָדָם וְאַחַת בָּאִילָן,
chunks.en: or two are made by a person and one is in the tree,
chunks.st: or if two are established on the ground by a person and one is in the tree,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה, וְאֵין עוֹלִין לָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
chunks.en: it is kosher, but we may not go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the sukka is fit, but one may not ascend and enter it on the first Festival day
chunks.stMore: because it is prohibited to use the tree.

chunks.en: If three are made by a person and one is in the tree,
chunks.st: However, if three of the walls are established on the ground by a person and one is in the tree,

chunks.en: it is kosher, and we may go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: then since it contains the minimum number of walls required, it is fit, and one may enter it on the first Festival day.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: The mishna summarizes that this is the principle:

chunks.en: any sukkah that, if the tree were taken away, could
chunks.st: Any case where, were the tree removed, the

chunks.en: stand up by itself,
chunks.st: sukka would be able to remain standing in and of itself,

chunks.en: is kosher, and we may go up into it on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: it is fit, and one may ascend and enter it on the Festival,
chunks.stMore: since the tree is not its primary support.

mishnayos.summary: Trees can be the walls of a sukkah. People busy with a mitzvah, sick people and those who take care of them do not have to sit in the sukkah. A small snack may be eaten outside the sukkah.

chunks.en: Someone who makes his sukkah between the trees,
chunks.st: In the case of one who establishes his sukka between the trees,

chunks.en: and the trees are its walls,
chunks.st: and the trees serve as walls for it,

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרָה. שְׁלוּחֵי מִצְוָה פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסֻּכָּה.
chunks.en: it is kosher. People on their way to do a mitzvah do not have to sit in the sukkah.
chunks.st: the sukka is fit. Those on the path to perform a mitzva are exempt from the mitzva of sukka.

chunks.en: Sick people and those who take care of them do not have to sit in the sukkah.
chunks.st: The ill and their caretakers are exempt from the mitzva of sukka.

chunks.en: We may eat and drink a snack outside the sukkah.
chunks.explain: A small snack, not a real meal.
chunks.st: One may eat and drink in the framework of a casual meal outside the sukka.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai and Rabban Gamliel ate even a little food in the sukkah. Rabbi Tzadok ate a tiny bit of food outside the sukkah and did not make a bracha after it.

chunks.en: Once, they brought to Rabban Yochanan
chunks.st: An incident occurred where they brought a cooked dish to Rabban Yoḥanan

chunks.en: ben Zakkai a cooked dish to taste,
chunks.st: ben Zakkai for him to taste,

words.note: A great leader of the Jewish people after the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed.

chunks.en: and to Rabban Gamliel two dates
chunks.st: and to Rabban Gamliel they brought two dates

chunks.en: and a bucket of water.
chunks.st: and a bucket of water.

chunks.en: And they said, "Take them up to the sukkah."
chunks.st: And they each said: Take them up to the sukka

chunks.en: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok
chunks.st: and we will eat them there. In contrast, the mishna relates: And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok

chunks.en: less than an egg's worth of food,
chunks.st: less than an egg-bulk of food,

words.en: than the size of an egg

chunks.en: he picked it up with a cloth,
chunks.explain: He did not wash his hands for such a small amount.
chunks.st: he took the food in a cloth
chunks.stMore: for cleanliness; he did not wash his hands because in his opinion, one is not required to wash his hands before eating less than an egg-bulk.

chunks.he: וַאֲכָלוֹ חוּץ לַסֻּכָּה, וְלֹא בֵרַךְ אַחֲרָיו:
chunks.en: and ate it outside the sukkah, and did not make a bracha after it.
chunks.st: And he ate it outside the sukka and did not recite a blessing after eating it.
chunks.stMore: He holds that one is not required to recite a blessing after eating less than an egg-bulk, as it is not satisfying, and it is written: “And you shall eat and be satisfied and bless the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 8:10). The Gemara will explain the halakhic rationale for each of these actions described.

mishnayos.stIntro: Apropos eating in the sukka, which is discussed in the previous mishna, this mishna relates:

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer says one must eat fourteen meals in the sukkah. The Sages say only the meal on the first night is a must. If you missed it, the Sages say it cannot be made up.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: fourteen meals a person must
chunks.st: A person is obligated to eat fourteen meals

words.note: Arba esrei means fourteen.

chunks.en: eat in the sukkah,
chunks.st: in the sukka over the course of the seven days of the festival of Sukkot,

chunks.en: one in the day and one at night.
chunks.st: one during the day each day and one at night each night.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: there is no set number,
chunks.st: There is no quota
chunks.stMore: for the number of meals, and one may choose whether or not to eat any of the meals

chunks.en: except for the night of the first Yom Tov
chunks.st: except for the meal on the evening of the first Festival day

chunks.en: of the chag, only.
chunks.st: of Sukkot,
chunks.stMore: which one is required to eat in the sukka.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Eliezer also said,
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer said:

chunks.en: someone who did not eat on the night of
chunks.st: One who did not eat

chunks.en: the first Yom Tov
chunks.st: a meal on the evening of the first day of the Festival

chunks.en: should make it up on the night of the last Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: The last Yom Tov is Shemini Atzeres.
chunks.st: should compensate with a meal on the evening of the last day of the Festival, on the Eighth Day of Assembly,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he will not eat it in the sukka.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: there is no making it up.
chunks.st: There is no compensation for this matter,

chunks.en: About this it says:
chunks.st: and with regard to similar cases where it is impossible to rectify failure to fulfill a positive mitzva, it is stated:

chunks.en: "What is crooked cannot be made straight,
chunks.st: “That which is crooked cannot be made straight;

chunks.en: and what is missing cannot be counted."
chunks.st: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered” (Ecclesiastes 1:15).

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about someone who sits with his head and most of his body in the sukkah while his table is in the house. They argue about a story with Rabbi Yochanan ben HaChoranis.

chunks.en: Someone whose head and most of his body were in the sukkah,
chunks.st: In the case of one whose head and most of his body were in the sukka

chunks.en: and his table was inside the house:
chunks.st: and his table was in the house,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is not kosher,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai deem it unfit,

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי,
chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to Beis Shammai,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: "Wasn't there a story like this?
chunks.st: And wasn’t there an incident

chunks.en: The Elders of Beis Shammai and the Elders of
chunks.st: where the Elders of Beit Shammai and the Elders of

chunks.en: Beis Hillel went to visit Rabbi
chunks.st: Beit Hillel went to visit Rabbi

chunks.en: Yochanan ben HaChoranis,
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben HaḤoranit

chunks.he: וּמְצָאוּהוּ שֶׁהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בַסֻּכָּה,
chunks.en: and they found him sitting with his head and most of his body in the sukkah,
chunks.st: and they found him such that he was sitting with his head and most of his body in the sukka

chunks.en: and his table inside the house,
chunks.st: and his table in the house,

chunks.en: and they did not say anything to him."
chunks.st: and they said nothing to him?
chunks.stMore: Even Beit Shammai did not object.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to them:

chunks.en: "Is that a proof?
chunks.st: Is there proof from there?
chunks.stMore: That is not what happened; rather,

chunks.en: They really said to him,
chunks.st: they said to him:

chunks.en: 'If this is how you always did it,
chunks.st: If you were accustomed to act in this manner,

chunks.en: you never kept the mitzvah of sukkah in your life!'"
chunks.st: you have never fulfilled the mitzva of sukka in your life.

mishnayos.summary: Women, servants and young children do not have to sit in the sukkah, but a child who no longer needs his mother must. Shammai made a sukkah over the bed for his new grandson.

chunks.en: Women, servants and young children
chunks.st: Women, slaves, and minors

chunks.en: do not have to sit in the sukkah.
chunks.st: are exempt from the mitzva of sukka.

chunks.en: A child who does not need his mother anymore
chunks.explain: He does not wake up calling for his mother.
chunks.st: A minor who does not need his mother any longer

chunks.en: must sit in the sukkah.
chunks.st: is obligated in the mitzva.

chunks.en: Once, the daughter-in-law of Shammai had a baby,
chunks.st: There was an incident where the daughter-in-law of Shammai

chunks.en: the Elder, and he broke open the plaster roof and put s'chach
chunks.st: the Elder gave birth just before Sukkot, and Shammai removed the coat of plaster from the roof, leaving the beams, and roofed with the beams

words.en: and he made a hole in

chunks.en: over the bed, for the baby.
chunks.st: over the bed for the newborn minor.

mishnayos.summary: During Sukkos, the sukkah is our main home. If it rains hard enough to spoil food, we may go inside. The rain is like a master who does not want his servant's service.

chunks.en: All seven days, a person makes
chunks.st: All seven days of Sukkot, a person renders

chunks.en: his sukkah his real home, and his house only for a short while.
chunks.st: his sukka his permanent residence and his house his temporary residence.

chunks.en: If rain fell,
chunks.st: If rain fell,

chunks.en: from when may he leave the sukkah?
chunks.st: from when is it permitted to vacate the sukka?

chunks.en: From when the rain would spoil a thick dish.
chunks.st: It is permitted from the point that it is raining so hard that the congealed dish will spoil.

words.note: A thick food, like porridge, that is spoiled by a little water.

chunks.en: They gave a parable:
chunks.st: The Sages told a parable:

chunks.en: what is this like?
chunks.st: To what is this matter comparable?

chunks.en: To a servant who came to pour a cup of wine for his master,
chunks.st: It is comparable to a servant who comes to pour wine for his master,

chunks.en: and his master poured a jug of water in his face.
chunks.explain: This shows the master does not want his service.
chunks.st: and he pours a jug [kiton] of water in his face to show him that his presence is not desired. So too, in the sukka, rain is an indication that the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not want the person to fulfill the mitzva of sukka.
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says clearly that it is the master who pours the water.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches which lulavim are not kosher: stolen, dried out, used for avodah zarah, or with a broken top or broken leaves. A lulav must be at least three tefachim long.

chunks.en: A lulav that is stolen or dried out
chunks.st: A lulav that was stolen or that is completely dry

chunks.he: פָּסוּל. שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת,
chunks.en: is not kosher. One from an asheirah tree or from a city that served idols
chunks.st: is unfit for use in fulfilling the mitzva of the four species. The lulav of a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira] and a lulav from a city whose residents were incited to idolatry,
chunks.stMore: which must be burned along with all the city’s property,

words.note: A tree that people worshipped as an idol.
A Jewish city where the people were led to serve idols.

chunks.en: is not kosher. If its top was cut off,
chunks.st: are unfit. If the top of the lulav was severed

chunks.en: or its leaves were broken off,
chunks.st: or if the palm leaves were severed from the spine of the lulav,

chunks.en: it is not kosher. If its leaves spread apart,
chunks.st: it is unfit. If its leaves, although still attached, were spread
chunks.stMore: and are no longer completely joined to the spine,

chunks.en: it is kosher. Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: it is fit. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: he should tie it together at the top.
chunks.st: In that case, one should bind the lulav from the top,
chunks.stMore: to join the leaves that spread to the spine.

chunks.en: Lulavim from the palms of the Iron Mountain are kosher.
chunks.explain: Their leaves are short and do not cover the whole spine.
chunks.st: A lulav from the palms of the Iron Mountain are fit
chunks.stMore: for use, although it differs from one taken from a standard palm tree, in that its leaves are shorter and do not cover the entire spine.

chunks.en: A lulav that is three tefachim long,
chunks.st: A lulav that has three handbreadths

chunks.en: enough to shake it, is kosher.
chunks.st: in length, sufficient to enable one to wave with it, is fit for use in fulfilling the mitzva.

mishnayos.summary: A hadas (myrtle branch) that is stolen, dried out, used for avodah zarah, or broken is not kosher. If it has more berries than leaves, it can be fixed by picking off berries, but not on Yom Tov.

chunks.en: A hadas that is stolen or dried out
chunks.st: A myrtle branch that was stolen or that is completely dry

words.note: A myrtle branch, one of the four minim.

chunks.he: פָּסוּל. שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת,
chunks.en: is not kosher. One from an asheirah tree or from a city that served idols
chunks.st: is unfit. A myrtle branch of a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira] or a myrtle branch from a city whose residents were incited to idolatry

chunks.en: is not kosher. If its top was cut off,
chunks.st: is unfit. If the top of the myrtle branch was severed,

chunks.en: or its leaves were broken off, or
chunks.st: if the leaves were severed completely, or if

chunks.en: its berries were more than its leaves,
chunks.st: its berries were more numerous than its leaves,

chunks.en: it is not kosher. But if he made them fewer,
chunks.explain: By picking off some berries.
chunks.st: it is unfit. If one diminished their number by plucking berries so that they no longer outnumbered the leaves,

chunks.en: it is kosher. But we may not make them fewer on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the myrtle branch is fit. But one may not diminish the number on the Festival itself.

mishnayos.summary: An aravah (willow branch) that is stolen, dried out, used for avodah zarah, or broken is not kosher. A tzaftzafa is not a real aravah. A wilted aravah, or one from a dry field, is kosher.

chunks.en: An aravah that is stolen or dried out
chunks.st: A willow branch that was stolen or is completely dry

words.note: A willow branch, one of the four minim.

chunks.he: פְּסוּלָה. שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת,
chunks.en: is not kosher. One from an asheirah tree or from a city that served idols
chunks.st: is unfit. One from a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira] or from a city whose residents were incited to idolatry

chunks.en: is not kosher. If its top was cut off,
chunks.st: is unfit. If the top was severed,

chunks.en: or its leaves were broken off,
chunks.st: or its leaves were severed,

chunks.en: or a tzaftzafa, it is not kosher.
chunks.explain: A tzaftzafa looks like a willow, but is a different kind of tree.
chunks.st: or if it is the tzaftzafa, a species similar to, but not actually a willow, it is unfit.

chunks.en: One that is wilted, or that lost a few of its leaves,
chunks.st: However, a willow branch that is slightly dried, and one that a minority of its leaves fell,

chunks.en: or that grew in a field without a river, is kosher.
chunks.explain: Most willows grow near rivers.
chunks.st: and a branch from a willow that does not grow by the river, but instead is from a non-irrigated field, is fit.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yishmael says we take three hadasim, two aravos, one lulav and one esrog. Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva disagree about how many we need and if they may be cut at the top.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: three hadasim and two aravos,
chunks.st: The mitzva of the four species is to take three myrtle branches, and two willow branches,

chunks.en: one lulav and one esrog,
chunks.st: one lulav, and one etrog.

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ שְׁנַיִם קְטוּמִים וְאֶחָד אֵינוֹ קָטוּם.
chunks.en: even if two hadasim are cut at the top and one is not cut.
chunks.st: With regard to the myrtle branches, even if the tops of two are severed and the top of one is not severed, it is fit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

chunks.en: even if all three are cut at the top.
chunks.st: Even if the tops of all three are severed, it is fit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says with regard to the number of each of the species:

chunks.en: just as there is one lulav and one esrog,
chunks.st: Just as there is one lulav and one etrog,

chunks.en: so there is one hadas and one aravah.
chunks.st: so too there is one myrtle branch and one willow branch.

mishnayos.summary: An esrog that is stolen, dried out, from avodah zarah, orlah or tamei terumah is not kosher. Some kinds of esrog should not be used at first, but if used they are kosher.

chunks.en: An esrog that is stolen or dried out
chunks.st: An etrog that was stolen or is completely dry

chunks.he: פָּסוּל. שֶׁל אֲשֵׁרָה וְשֶׁל עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת,
chunks.en: is not kosher. One from an asheirah tree or from a city that served idols
chunks.st: is unfit. One from a tree worshipped as idolatry [asheira] or from a city whose residents were incited to idolatry

chunks.en: is not kosher. One that is orlah
chunks.explain: Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden.
chunks.st: is unfit. An etrog that is fruit that grew on a tree during the three years after it was planted [orla]

chunks.en: is not kosher. One of terumah that is tamei
chunks.st: is unfit, because it is prohibited to eat and derive benefit from it. An etrog of impure teruma

words.note: A gift of food for the Kohanim.

chunks.en: is not kosher. One of terumah that is tahor:
chunks.st: is unfit. With regard to an etrog of pure teruma,

chunks.en: he should not take it,
chunks.st: one may not take it ab initio,

chunks.en: but if he took it,
chunks.st: and if one took it,

chunks.en: it is kosher. One of demai:
chunks.explain: Demai is food bought from someone who may not have taken off ma'aser.
chunks.st: it is fit, and he fulfilled his obligation after the fact. With regard to an etrog of demai,
chunks.stMore: which is produce acquired from an am ha’aretz, who does not reliably tithe his produce,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is not kosher,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai deem it unfit,

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is kosher.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel deem it fit.

chunks.en: One of ma'aser sheni in Yerushalayim:
chunks.explain: Ma'aser sheni is a tenth of the crops, eaten in Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: With regard to an etrog of second tithe in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: he should not take it,
chunks.st: one may not take it ab initio;

chunks.en: but if he took it, it is kosher.
chunks.st: and if he took it, it is fit.

mishnayos.summary: An esrog with spots on most of it, or that lost its tip, or is peeled, split or has a hole with a piece missing, is not kosher. A black esrog is not kosher, and Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda argue about a green one.

chunks.en: If spots grew over most of it,
chunks.st: If boil-like blemishes arose on the majority of the etrog;

chunks.en: if its pitam was taken off,
chunks.explain: The pitam is the little tip at the top of the esrog.
chunks.st: if its pestle-like protuberance on the upper, blossom end was removed;

chunks.en: if it was peeled, if it was split,
chunks.st: if the etrog was peeled, split,

chunks.en: or it has a hole and is missing any bit,
chunks.st: or pierced and is missing any amount,

chunks.en: it is not kosher. If spots grew over a small part of it,
chunks.st: it is unfit. However, if boil-like blemishes arose only on its minority;

chunks.en: if its stem was taken off,
chunks.st: if its stem, which connects it to the tree, was removed;

chunks.en: or it has a hole but nothing is missing,
chunks.st: or it was pierced but is not missing any amount,

chunks.en: it is kosher. A black esrog
chunks.st: it is fit. A Cushite etrog,
chunks.stMore: which is black like a Cushite,

chunks.en: is not kosher. And one as green as a leek:
chunks.st: is unfit. And with regard to an etrog that is leek green,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says it is kosher,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems it fit

chunks.en: and Rabbi Yehuda says it is not kosher.
chunks.st: and Rabbi Yehuda deems it unfit.

mishnayos.summary: How small or how big may an esrog be? Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei give different sizes.

chunks.en: The smallest size of an esrog:
chunks.st: What is the minimum measure of a small etrog?

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: like a walnut. Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: It may be no smaller than a walnut-bulk. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: like an egg. And the biggest size:
chunks.st: It may be no smaller than an egg-bulk. And in a large

chunks.en: small enough to hold two in one hand,
chunks.st: etrog, the maximum measure is so that one could hold two in his one hand;

chunks.en: says Rabbi Yehuda.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: even if he can hold only one with both hands.
chunks.st: It is fit even if it is so large that he can hold only one in his two hands.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yehuda says the lulav must be tied with something from its own kind. Rabbi Meir says any string is fine, and tells about the people of Yerushalayim who used gold bands.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: And where did they shake the lulav?
chunks.st: And where in the recitation of hallel would they wave the lulav?

chunks.st: They would do so at the verse: “Thank the Lord, for He is good” (Psalms 118:1, 29) that appears at both the beginning and the end of the psalm,

chunks.en: and at "Ana Hashem hoshi'ah na,"
chunks.explain: This means "Please, Hashem, save us."
chunks.st: and at the verse: “Lord, please save us” (Psalms 118:25);

chunks.en: says Beis Hillel.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Beit Hillel.

chunks.en: And Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: And Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: also at "Ana Hashem hatzlichah na."
chunks.explain: This means "Please, Hashem, give us success."
chunks.st: They would wave the lulav even at the verse: “Lord, please grant us success” (Psalms 118:25).

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.he: צוֹפֶה הָיִיתִי בְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּבְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
chunks.en: I watched Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua:
chunks.st: I was observing Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua

chunks.he: שֶׁכָּל הָעָם הָיוּ מְנַעְנְעִים אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן,

chunks.st: and saw that all the people were waving their lulavim,

chunks.st: “Lord, please save us,”

chunks.st: have a lulav in his hand to take
chunks.stMore: and fulfill the mitzva while traveling,

chunks.en: when he comes into his house, he should take it at his table.
chunks.st: when he enters his house to eat,he should take the lulav at his table.
chunks.stMore: He interrupts his meal to fulfill the mitzva of lulav.

chunks.en: If he did not take it in the morning,
chunks.st: If he did not take the lulav in the morning,

chunks.en: he should take it in the afternoon,
chunks.st: he should take it in the afternoon,

chunks.en: because the whole day is good for the lulav.

mishnayos.summary: If someone cannot say Hallel by himself, and a servant, woman or child says it for him, he must repeat every word. If a grown man says it for him, he just answers "Halleluyah."

chunks.en: Someone for whom a servant or a woman
chunks.st: With regard to one for whom a Canaanite slave, a woman,

chunks.en: or a child was saying Hallel,
chunks.st: or a minor was reciting hallel,

chunks.en: must repeat after them what they say.
chunks.st: he repeats after them what they are saying word for word.

chunks.en: And a curse should come on him!
chunks.explain: For not learning to say it himself.
chunks.st: The mishna notes: And may a curse come to him
chunks.stMore: for being so ignorant that he needs them to recite it for him.

chunks.en: If a grown man was saying it for him,
chunks.st: If an adult male was reciting hallel on his
chunks.stMore: behalf, he need not repeat each word, as the adult male can fulfill the obligation to recite hallel on his behalf. Rather,

chunks.en: he answers after him "Halleluyah."
chunks.st: he simply answers: Halleluya, to each phrase that is recited.

mishnayos.summary: In saying Hallel and its bracha, everyone follows the custom of his place. During shemittah, someone buying a lulav from a person who may not keep shemittah gets the esrog as a gift.

chunks.en: In a place where they are used to repeating verses,
chunks.st: In a place where they were accustomed to repeat certain verses,

chunks.en: he should repeat them. To say them once,
chunks.st: he, too, should repeat them. If the custom is to recite them plainly,

chunks.en: he should say them once. To make a bracha after it,
chunks.st: without repetition, he should recite them plainly. In a place where the custom is to recite a blessing after hallel,

chunks.en: he should make a bracha after it.
chunks.st: he should recite a blessing.

chunks.en: Everything follows the custom of the place.
chunks.st: Everything is in accordance with the local custom in these matters.

chunks.en: Someone who buys a lulav from his friend in the shemittah year
chunks.explain: Shemittah is the seventh year, when fruit may not be bought and sold like usual.
chunks.st: In the case of one who purchases a lulav from another who is an am ha’aretz during the Sabbatical Year,

chunks.en: should get the esrog as a gift,
chunks.st: the seller gives him an etrog along with it as a gift,

chunks.en: because he may not buy it in shemittah.
chunks.st: as he is not permitted to purchase the etrog during the Sabbatical Year because it is prohibited to engage in commerce with Sabbatical-Year produce.

mishnayos.summary: In the time of the Beis HaMikdash, the lulav was taken all seven days only in the Beis HaMikdash. After it was destroyed, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule to take it everywhere for seven days, to remember the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה לוּלָב נִטָּל בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ שִׁבְעָה,
chunks.en: At first, the lulav was taken in the Beis HaMikdash for seven days,
chunks.st: Originally, during the Temple era, the lulav was taken in the Temple for seven days,

chunks.en: and everywhere else for one day.
chunks.st: and in the rest of the country outside the Temple it was taken for one day.

chunks.en: When the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
chunks.st: Once the Temple was destroyed,

chunks.en: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a rule
chunks.st: Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted an ordinance

chunks.en: that the lulav should be taken everywhere for seven days,
chunks.st: that the lulav should be taken even in the rest of the country for seven days,

chunks.en: to remember the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: in commemoration of the Temple.

chunks.en: And that the whole day of waving the omer should be forbidden.
chunks.explain: On that day we may not eat from the new grain.
chunks.st: And for similar reasons, he instituted an ordinance that for the entire day of waving the omer offering, it should be prohibited to eat the grain of the new crop.
chunks.stMore: It is prohibited to eat the grain of the new crop until the omer offering is brought and waved in the Temple on the sixteenth of Nisan. The offering was sacrificed in the morning; however, after taking potential delays into consideration, the new crop remained prohibited until it was clear that the offering had been sacrificed. Practically speaking, it was prohibited to eat the new grain until the sixteenth of Nisan was over; it was permitted only on the seventeenth. Once the Temple was destroyed and there was no longer an omer offering sacrificed, it was permitted to eat the new crop on the sixteenth. However, Rabban Yoḥanan instituted an ordinance that eating the new grain would remain prohibited until the seventeenth to commemorate the Temple.

words.note: The day the omer offering was waved in the Beis HaMikdash.

mishnayos.summary: When the first day of Sukkos is on Shabbos, people bring their lulavim to shul before Shabbos. On the first day a person must use his own lulav, but on the other days he may use his friend's.

chunks.en: The first day of
chunks.st: If the first day of

chunks.en: the chag, if it falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: the festival of Sukkot occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: all the people bring
chunks.st: all of the people bring their

chunks.en: their lulavim to the shul.
chunks.explain: They bring them before Shabbos, since we may not carry outside on Shabbos.
chunks.st: lulavim to the synagogue
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat eve, as it is prohibited to carry in a public domain on Shabbat.

words.note: Beis haknesses is the shul.

chunks.en: The next day, they come early,
chunks.st: The next day, on Shabbat, everyone rises early and comes to the synagogue.

chunks.he: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מַכִּיר אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ,
chunks.en: and each one finds his own lulav
chunks.st: Each and every one recognizes his lulav

chunks.en: and takes it. Because the Sages said,
chunks.st: and takes it. This emphasis that each and every one recognizes his own lulav and takes it is because the Sages said:

chunks.st: A person does not fulfill his obligation to take the lulav

chunks.en: on the first day of the chag
chunks.st: on the first day of the Festival

chunks.en: with his friend's lulav.
chunks.st: with the lulav of another,

chunks.en: But on the other days of the chag,
chunks.st: and on the rest of the days of the Festival

chunks.en: a person does his mitzvah
chunks.st: a person fulfills his obligation

chunks.en: with his friend's lulav.
chunks.st: even with the lulav of another.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yosei says that if someone forgot it was Shabbos and carried his lulav outside, he does not need to bring a korban, because he was busy with a mitzvah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: the first day of
chunks.st: If the first day of

chunks.en: the chag, if it falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: the Festival occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: and he forgot and carried the lulav out to a public place,
chunks.st: and he forgot and carried the lulav out into the public domain,

chunks.en: he does not have to bring a korban, because he carried it with permission.
chunks.explain: He was busy with the mitzvah of lulav.
chunks.st: he is exempt from liability to bring a sin-offering for this unwitting transgression because he carried it out with permission,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he was preoccupied with the performance of the mitzva and carried it out.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos and Yom Tov we may put the lulav back in water to keep it fresh. A child who knows how to shake the lulav must take one.

chunks.en: A woman may take the lulav from her son or from
chunks.st: A woman may receive a lulav from her son or from

chunks.en: her husband, and put it back in the water on Shabbos.
chunks.st: her husband and return it on Shabbat to the water in which it had been placed.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: on Shabbos we put it back,
chunks.st: On Shabbat one may return the lulav to the water;

chunks.en: on Yom Tov we may add water,
chunks.st: and on the Festival one may even add fresh water to the vessel so the lulav will not wilt;

chunks.en: and on Chol HaMoed we may change the water.
chunks.st: and during the intermediate days of the Festival, one may even change the water.

chunks.en: A child who knows how to shake the lulav
chunks.st: A minor who knows how to wave the lulav

chunks.en: must take the lulav.
chunks.explain: So that he learns to do mitzvos.
chunks.st: is obligated in the mitzva of lulav due to the requirement to train him in the performance of mitzvot.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the mitzvos of Sukkos and for how many days each one is done: lulav and aravah, Hallel and simcha, sukkah and pouring water on the mizbe'ach, and the flute.

chunks.en: The lulav and the aravah:
chunks.st: The lulav is taken and the altar is encircled together with the willow branch

chunks.en: six or seven days.
chunks.explain: It depends on which day is Shabbos.
chunks.st: either six or seven days,
chunks.stMore: depending on which day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat.

chunks.en: Hallel and the simcha:
chunks.explain: Simcha here means eating from the korban shelamim.
chunks.st: The obligation to recite the full hallel and the mitzva of rejoicing,
chunks.stMore: i.e., eating the meat of the peace-offering,

chunks.en: eight days. The sukkah and pouring the water on the mizbe'ach:
chunks.st: is in effect for eight days, seven days of Sukkot and the Eighth Day of Assembly. The mitzva of sukka and the ritual of the water libation

chunks.en: five or six days.
chunks.st: is played in the Temple for five or six days,
chunks.stMore: depending on which day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat, to enhance the rejoicing on the Festival.

mishnayos.summary: We take the lulav for seven days only when the first day of Sukkos is on Shabbos. Otherwise it is six days, because we do not take it on a Shabbos in the middle of Sukkos.

chunks.en: How is the lulav seven days?
chunks.st: The lulav is taken for seven days. How so?

chunks.en: If the first day of
chunks.st: If the first day of

chunks.en: the chag falls on Shabbos,
chunks.explain: On the first day the lulav is a mitzvah from the Torah, so we take it even on Shabbos.
chunks.st: the Festival occurs on Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: since the mitzva to take the lulav on the first day is a mitzva by Torah law, it overrides Shabbat and one takes the lulav that day.

chunks.en: the lulav is seven days.
chunks.st: As a result, the lulav is then taken for seven days.

chunks.en: And on all the other days, six.
chunks.explain: Then one of the other days is Shabbos, and we do not take the lulav.
chunks.st: And if the first day occurs on one of the rest of the days of the week and one of the other days of the Festival coincides with Shabbat, the lulav is taken only six days.
chunks.stMore: Since the mitzva to take the lulav is a mitzva by rabbinic law throughout the rest of Sukkot, it does not override Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: The aravah is done for seven days only when the seventh day of Sukkos is on Shabbos. Otherwise it is six days.

chunks.en: How is the aravah seven days?
chunks.st: The altar is encircled with the willow branch for seven days. How so?

chunks.en: If the seventh day of the aravah
chunks.st: If the seventh day of the mitzva of the willow branch

chunks.en: falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: occurs on Shabbat,
chunks.stMore: since on that day it is a mitzva by Torah law, it overrides Shabbat

chunks.en: the aravah is seven days.
chunks.st: and the mitzva of the willow branch is then performed for seven days.

chunks.en: And on all the other days, six.
chunks.st: And if the seventh day occurs on one of the rest of the days of the week, and one of the other days of the Festival coincides with Shabbat, since the mitzva of the willow branch is then by rabbinic law and consequently does not override Shabbat, it is performed for only six days.

mishnayos.summary: When the first day of Sukkos was on Shabbos, people left their lulavim on the Har HaBayis. Grabbing for them in the morning became dangerous, so the beis din made a rule that everyone takes the lulav at home.

chunks.en: How was the mitzvah of lulav done?
chunks.st: How is the mitzva of lulav fulfilled in the Temple when the first day of the Festival occurs on Shabbat?

chunks.en: If the first day of
chunks.st: If the first day of

chunks.en: the chag fell on Shabbos,
chunks.st: the Festival occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: they bring their lulavim to the Har HaBayis.
chunks.explain: They bring them before Shabbos.
chunks.st: all the people bring their lulavim to the Temple Mount

chunks.en: The helpers take them from them and line them up
chunks.st: on Friday. The attendants receive the lulavim from them and arrange

chunks.en: on top of a bench.
chunks.st: them on a bench [itztaba],

chunks.explain: So they will not get pushed in the crowd the next morning.
chunks.st: while the Elders place their lulavim in the chamber.

chunks.en: And they teach them to say,
chunks.st: And the court teaches the people to say:

chunks.st: With regard to anyone whom my lulav reaches his possession,

chunks.explain: Because on the first day one needs his own lulav.
chunks.st: it is his as a gift.
chunks.stMore: They did so to avoid the likely situation where people would inadvertently take lulavim that did not belong to them, as on the first day of the Festival one does not fulfill his obligation with a lulav that does not belong to him.

chunks.en: The next day, they come early,
chunks.st: The next day everyone rises early and comes to the Temple,

chunks.en: and the helpers throw the lulavim in front of them.
chunks.st: and the attendants throw the lulavim before them.

chunks.he: וְהֵן מְחַטְּפִין וּמַכִּין אִישׁ אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ.

chunks.st: And when the court saw that they came to potential danger,

chunks.en: they made a rule that each and every person
chunks.st: they instituted that each and every

chunks.st: person will take his lulav in his house and fulfill the mitzva there.

mishnayos.summary: The aravah was done in the Beis HaMikdash: they brought big willow branches from Motza, stood them around the mizbe'ach, blew the shofar, and walked around the mizbe'ach while davening. On the seventh day they walked around seven times.

chunks.st: There was a place below Jerusalem,

chunks.st: and it was called Motza.

chunks.st: They would descend there and gather

chunks.st: On the eighth day, when there was a completely different configuration of offerings, they returned to the standard lottery system used to determine which of the priestly watches would sacrifice the offerings, as they did on the other pilgrimage Festivals,
chunks.stMore: which do not have as many offerings as does Sukkot.

chunks.en: They said, a group that brought bulls today
chunks.st: They said about the ordering of the priestly watches: One who sacrificed bulls today

chunks.en: should not bring bulls tomorrow,
chunks.st: will not sacrifice bulls tomorrow;

chunks.en: but they take turns, round and round.
chunks.st: rather, they will sacrifice one of the other types of offerings. They rotate,
chunks.stMore: so that each of the watches will have the opportunity to sacrifice bulls as well as other animals.

mishnayos.summary: On the three Regalim, all twenty-four groups of Kohanim share the korbanos and the lechem hapanim. But the group whose week it is still brings the regular korbanos.

chunks.he: בִּשְׁלשָׁה פְרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה הָיוּ כָּל מִשְׁמָרוֹת
chunks.en: Three times a year all the groups of Kohanim were
chunks.st: At three times during the year, all twenty-four priestly watches

chunks.he: שָׁווֹת בְּאֵמוּרֵי הָרְגָלִים וּבְחִלּוּק לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים.
chunks.en: equal in the korbanos of the Yom Tov and in sharing the lechem hapanim.
chunks.explain: The lechem hapanim is the special bread on the Shulchan in the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: have equal status, in that all receive a share in the Temple service independent of the standard order of the watches and all receive a share in the accompanying gifts of the priesthood: In the portions of the offerings of the Festivals sacrificed on the altar and in the distribution of the shewbread on Shabbat during the Festivals.

chunks.en: On Shavuos they say to each Kohen,
chunks.st: On Shavuot that coincides with Shabbat, when the two loaves offered on Shavuot would be distributed together with the distribution of the shewbread, the priest charged with the distribution says to each priest:

words.note: Atzeres is Shavuos.

chunks.en: "Here is matzah, here is chametz."
chunks.explain: The lechem hapanim was matzah, and the special Shavuos bread was chametz.
chunks.st: Here is matza from the shewbread for you, and here is leavened bread from the two loaves for you.

chunks.en: The group whose time is set,
chunks.st: The principle is that the priestly watch whose time is fixed during the Festival

chunks.en: brings the korban tamid,
chunks.st: sacrifices the daily offerings

chunks.en: korbanos people promised or gave, and the other korbanos of the public,
chunks.st: during the Festival, as well as vow-offerings, free-will offerings, and all other communal offerings.

chunks.en: and it brings all of them.
chunks.st: And that watch sacrifices all of them
chunks.stMore: even during the Festival, when other aspects of the service are shared by all the watches.

chunks.en: A Yom Tov that is right next to Shabbos,
chunks.st: In the case of a Festival that occurs adjacent to Shabbat,

chunks.en: whether before it or after it,
chunks.st: both when it occurs preceding it and when it occurs following it,

chunks.en: all the groups were equal
chunks.st: all the watches that arrived early or remained late to serve in the Temple were of equal status

chunks.en: in sharing the lechem hapanim.
chunks.st: in the distribution of the shewbread on that Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells how the lechem hapanim was split between groups of Kohanim. The group of Bilga was given a punishment: it always shared in the south, its ring was fixed and its cubby was closed.

chunks.he: חָל לִהְיוֹת יוֹם אֶחָד לְהַפְסִיק בֵּינְתַיִם,
chunks.en: If there happened to be one day in between,
chunks.explain: One day between Yom Tov and Shabbos.
chunks.st: If one day happened to separate between the Festival and Shabbat,

chunks.en: the group whose time is set,
chunks.st: the watch whose time was scheduled

chunks.en: would take ten loaves,
chunks.st: would take ten of the twelve loaves of shewbread,

chunks.en: and the group that stayed later takes two.
chunks.explain: They stayed because there was no time to get home before Shabbos.
chunks.st: and the watch that was detained after the Festival because there was insufficient time to get home before Shabbat takes two loaves.

chunks.en: And on the rest of the days of the year,
chunks.st: And during the rest of the days of the year,
chunks.stMore: when the changing of the watches takes place on Shabbat,

chunks.en: the group coming in takes six,
chunks.st: the incoming watch takes six loaves

chunks.en: and the group going out takes six.
chunks.st: and the outgoing watch takes six loaves.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: the group coming in takes seven,
chunks.st: The incoming watch takes seven loaves

chunks.en: and the group going out takes five.
chunks.st: and the outgoing takes five.

chunks.en: The ones coming in share them in the north,
chunks.st: The standard procedure was that the members of the incoming watch divide the shewbread in the north section of the courtyard,

chunks.en: and the ones going out in the south.
chunks.st: and the outgoing watch in the south.

chunks.en: The group of Bilga always shares in the south,
chunks.explain: This was a punishment for the group of Bilga.
chunks.st: However, there was one exception: The watch of Bilga, due to a penalty imposed upon it, always divides the shewbread to its members in the south,

chunks.en: and its ring is fixed in place,
chunks.explain: They could not use their ring when preparing korbanos.
chunks.st: even when it is the incoming watch. And its ring used to facilitate slaughter of the animals was fixed in place,
chunks.stMore: rendering it useless,

chunks.en: and its cubby is closed up.
chunks.explain: Each group kept its knives and tools in a cubby in the wall.
chunks.st: and its niche among the niches in the wall of the Chamber of Knives, where the priests would store their knives and other vessels, was sealed.
